title: Replicating 'larger models are more steerable' as a within-family scaling curve

original_idea.body: Take one safety concept and CAA, measure steering effectiveness across Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B, and run an explicit monotonicity test of the steerability-vs-scale claim within one family.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: scaling of steerability shapes future-control expectations, but within-family replication with a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: One concept, one method, size sweep; beginner-verifiable.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Replication of a published scaling claim; labs also cover scaling.

novelty.reasoning: Direct within-family replication of an established finding; largely addressed.
